# K8.4 Residual-stream gradient sums in the RMSNorm backward; MLP residual in the unpermute

Classification: Internal (becomes public with the MLPerf Training v6.1 results)

[Index](../KERNELS.md) · Switches: `NVFP4_RESGRAD=1`, `NVFP4_RESGRAD_FWD=0`,
`NVFP4_RESGRAD_ROUTER=1` (`config_GB300_2x4x3xtp1pp1cp1ep1_nvfp4_v7.sh` L136-139) ·
Class: **Bitwise** (against K5.3 plus separate adds) · Rule basis: TR-8.3

## 1. Packages

G3, G6 and G6b, where named below, are Firmus's earlier GPT-OSS NVFP4 packages (`nemo_g3_nvfp4_v1`, `nemo_g6_nvfp4_v2`,
`nemo_g6b_nvfp4_v2_1`), withdrawn from this submission and no longer in this repository. Their values, line numbers,
images and test jobs are cited as the record of where evidence was collected ([Index](../KERNELS.md), "Earlier packages").

| | G6, G6b, G6c |
|---|---|
| Switches | `NVFP4_RESGRAD=1` (L136), `NVFP4_RESGRAD_FWD=0` (L137), `NVFP4_RESGRAD_ROUTER=1` (L139) |
| Requires | K5.3 (`NVFP4_TRITON_RMSNORM_BWD`), K3.3 (`NVFP4_FUSED_PERMUTE_PAD`); in G6c `NVFP4_RESGRAD_FWD=0` (K3.4 and K5.4 are off) and K10.3 adds the MLP residual in the unpermute instead |
| Code | V7 patch `nvfp4_resgrad.py` L1952-2357; `pretrain.py` L108-113 |

Same files in both packages and the same V7 patch in G6c.

## 2. What the reference does

A layer input `h` feeds the residual add and the RMSNorm in front of the sublayer, so autograd
adds `d_residual + d_norm` with a separate BF16 add over [tokens, hidden]. The pre-MLP norm
output feeds the router and the token permutation, so its two gradients are added the same way.
In the forward, the MLP residual is added after the unpermute (Megatron bias-dropout-add).

## 3. What this implementation does

1. `install` (L2267-2357) replaces `tex.rmsnorm_bwd` and the RMSNorm op's binding with
   `make_rmsnorm_bwd` (L2089-2128) and Megatron's `_bias_dropout_add_func` with `bda`
   (L2286-2302).
2. Backward of a residual add (`_ResidualAdd`, `_BiasResidualAdd`, `_PreAdded`; L2214-2264)
   hands its gradient to the RMSNorm backward of the same tensor, keyed by storage, offset,
   numel and dtype (`hand_over`, `_key`; L1989-2011).
3. `_rmsnorm_bwd_res_kernel` (L2043-2078) computes K5.3's dx, rounds it to BF16, adds the
   handed-over residual gradient in FP32 and rounds again (L2072-2075).
4. Router (`NVFP4_RESGRAD_ROUTER`): the router's input gradient is handed over by `_TapGrad`
   (L2018-2040) and summed into dz as `bf16(dz + dz2)` before use (L2062-2064).
5. Forward (`NVFP4_RESGRAD_FWD`): the K3.4 unpermute also adds the MLP residual,
   `bf16(residual + bf16(sum))` (L2131-2171, wrapper L2178-2211).
   Off in G6c; K10.3's no-bias unpermute
   records its output in the same `_preadded` map, and `bda` returns it through `_PreAdded` (L2214-2226, L2288-2293),
   which hands the residual gradient over as in step 2. With no linear bias, the attention residual add takes the
   no-bias `_ResidualAdd` path (L2298-2299).

## 4. Why the result is the same

Each fused sum is rounded exactly as the PyTorch BF16 add it replaces: both operands are BF16,
the add is done in FP32 and rounded once (L2063-2064, L2074-2075, L2169-2170). Addition is
commutative, so the operand order does not matter. The dx term uses an explicit `tl.fma`
(L2070-2072) so the compiler contracts the same terms as K5.3's kernel. Bitwise against K5.3
plus separate adds. Against TE's `rmsnorm_bwd` plus adds the result differs by K5.3's own
rounding (Same function, see K5.3).

## 5. Numerics

BF16 storage, FP32 arithmetic per row; dgamma through per-program FP32 partials reduced by K5.3's
`_reduce_rows_kernel` (L2112-2124); `NVFP4_RMSNORM_BWD_STAGES` (K5.3's switch) sets the pipeline
stages (L1982).

## 6. Shapes and fallbacks

- **Gate:** `install` raises unless K5.3 is installed (L2276-2277), `NVFP4_RMSNORM_BWD_UNROLL=1`
  (L2278-2279); the router part needs `NVFP4_FUSED_PERMUTE_PAD=1` with padding (L2317-2320); the
  forward part needs `NVFP4_DEFER_FC2_BIAS=1` and `NVFP4_UNPERMUTE_BIAS_UNROLL>0` (L2340-2343).
  Per call: `bda` fuses only in training with grad and a residual that requires grad
  (L2294-2295), with K5.4's `eligible` for the bias path or dropout 0 and equal shape/dtype for
  the no-bias path (L2296-2299); the unpermute only with no merging probs, a pending expert bias,
  matching residual size, dtype and contiguity (L2184-2196).
- **Falls back:** to the original bias-dropout-add (L2300), the original unpermute (L2196-2197)
  or K5.3's plain backward when nothing is pending for the input (L2098-2099). Silent; the
  counters in `_stats` (L1985) are not printed.
- **Assumes:** that the storage key identifies one tensor between forward and backward, and that
  every handed-over gradient is consumed by the norm backward of that tensor. This is checked:
  `check_empty` at the start of layer 1's forward raises if anything is left (L1994-2003,
  L2304-2311); a double hand-over raises (L2008-2009, L2028-2029); a pre-added unpermute output
  reaching another add raises (L2290-2292).
- **Check:** config L136-139; `NVFP4_RESGRAD installed (router 1, fwd 0)` and
  `FIRMUS resgrad fwd (no bias) installed (unroll 4)` (K10.3) in all 10 `results/firmus_gb300_ngpu8_gptoss_g6c_nvfp4_v2_2/gpt_oss_20b/result_*.txt` (L219, L220).
  A leftover gradient would end the run with a traceback;
  none of the 10 has one.

## 7. Code

- V7 patch `nvfp4_resgrad.py` L1952-2357; `nemo_g6c_nvfp4_v2_2/pretrain.py` L108-113 (after K5.3 at L49-60; the K5.4 block at
  L89-106 is off); K10.3's install follows at L115-119.
- Loaded through `_v7_module` (V7 patch L338-356); image verify jobs 22541 and 22589 on the G6b image (same patches and `Dockerfile`; not repeated on this image):
  `nvfp4_resgrad.py == production overlay` (record available on request).

## 8. Tests and evidence

Kernel tests on the image (Firmus test scripts, available on request; they import the
installed module):
- On this package's image: `k8_4_resgrad_module`, job 22919, modules built as this package's model (no bias,
  `../KERNELS.md` section 9): 8 cases, 0 with a difference; run a vs b 64 digests equal, 0 differ.
  `k5_3_k8_4_rmsnorm_bwd`, job 22884: K8.4 kernel vs K5.3 plus separate adds 0 elements differ, also with Inf/NaN in
  dz; vs TE `rmsnorm_bwd` plus adds 20-378 elements in the cases with a difference (K5.3's rounding); fixture
  (residual added before the backward) 70 775 709 elements; run a vs b 125 equal, 0 differ. The forward part of
  this package is K10.3's (test `k10_3_resgrad_fwd_nobias`). The G6 results follow.

- `k8_4_resgrad_module`, job 22461, 8 cases per run: a chain of TE `LayerNormLinear` (RMSNorm),
  `Linear`, bias-dropout-add, `RMSNorm`, `Linear`, add on [4096, 3, 2880], BF16 and NVFP4,
  install vs not installed (K5.3 in both): 0 cases differ (h1, h2, dh0, every parameter
  gradient). Run a vs run b: 80 equal, 0 differ. The router and forward parts need the MoE layer
  and are not in this test.
- `k5_3_k8_4_rmsnorm_bwd`, job 22434: K8.4 kernel vs K5.3 plus separate adds 0 elements differ
  (also with Inf/NaN in dz). Vs TE `rmsnorm_bwd` plus adds: 20-378 elements of dx (70 781 760)
  and dgamma together on finite inputs (job 22412: dx 17-378, dgamma 0-4); this is K5.3's
  rounding, by design of this comparison. Fixture (residual added before the
  backward): 70 775 709 elements. Run a vs run b: 343 equal, 0 differ.
- `k3_4_unpermute_bias`, job 22168 (forward part): `specials:plain` and `specials:resgrad` 0
  differ; the one case with a difference is K3.4's fixture. `k5_4_bias_residual`, job 22168:
  the bias path through `make_bias_residual_add`, K5.4's fixture only. The 2 differing run a vs
  run b digests in each are special-value inputs that were not identical between runs before job
  22242.
- **Training A/B**: `NVFP4_RESGRAD*=0` (22254) max |loss diff|
  0.1111 to base; base vs base 0.0873-0.1192.
